subject: research/chip-systolic-hidewide
professional: a senior computer-architecture researcher who works on DNN accelerator dataflows (the kind who reviews for ISCA/MICRO/HPCA and knows SCALE-Sim, Timeloop/Accelergy, Eyeriss and the TPU papers). They would check first that the RTL is bit-exact against the reference, that the measured cycle counts match the textbook output-stationary fill/drain formula, that the area x delay metric is computed right, and then whether the comparison can express what a systolic array is for (operand reuse that cuts memory traffic) or only measures pipeline fill/drain on a tiny layer

evidence.correctness: Full rerun in a private copy with the same tool versions (Yosys 0.33 2584903a060, Icarus 12.0; `cd <scratch>/copy/chip-systolic-hidewide && PYTHONPATH=src /usr/bin/python3.13 experiments/run.py`, 3m27s) reproduced experiments/results.txt byte for byte (`diff` empty, all 8 arrays rtl==numpy True). Independent recomputation (`python3 /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/01e5da05-ab88-5d76-a2fd-1c01bbfb65e9/scratchpad/chip/indep.py <results.txt>`, which imports nothing from the subject): textbook output-stationary cycle count (Kung skew, PE(i,j) consumes operand k at t=k+i+j, compute K+R+C-2 cycles + 1 parallel write-back per tile, ceil(N/C) tiles) equals all 8 array cycle counts; the MAC-lane schedule ceil(N/P)*(K+1)+2 equals all 6 MAC cycle counts; cells x cycles / R recomputed equals all 14 metric values; ratios 1.2991 -> 1.30 and 1.2699 -> 1.27 match. SCALE-Sim's OS fold formula (2R+C+K-2, outputs drained through the array) agrees for R=1 and differs by 3 cycles for 2x8 only because this RTL reads accumulators out in parallel. Beyond the README: I simulated the MAC engine's RTL at F=16 and F=32 for P=4,8,16 (the README says those cycles came from the formula only) and off-sweep arrays 3x3@F=16, 2x5@F=20, 4x2@F=32 (`extra_sim.py`): all bit-exact against NumPy with Icarus cycles equal to the textbook formula. Numbers are right; one comparison sentence in the README is wrong (claims).
evidence.completeness: Everything the Method and Results sections say was done is present and runs: F-16-4 network, 4 arrays x 2 F, P=4/8/16, 32-vector Icarus check per array, Yosys generic-gate scoring, results.txt, figure.py/best_design.svg, reproduce block (`PYTHONPATH=src /usr/bin/python3.13 -m unittest discover -s tests`: 6 tests OK in 28.6 s, README says about 30 s; experiment 3m27s, README 'a few minutes'). Live page https://marisstella.app/research/chip-systolic-hidewide/ returns 200 with 1.30/1.27. Next steps are listed as not done (and were done by later projects chip-systolic-p32 and chip-mac-lanes).
evidence.verification: 6 tests OK in 28.6 s. The tests are real end-to-end checks (Icarus RTL vs integer NumPy at F=8 and 16, measured cycles vs formula, MAC engine at F=8/16), and they caught a one-cycle-late RUN end (gen.py:101) and an off-by-one in the MAC cycle formula (baseline_gen.py:16). 5 of 7 non-equivalent seeded mutants survived (quality_mutate.py): dropping the /R in the headline metric (experiments/run.py:35; run.py has no test at all), subtracting flip-flops from the Yosys cell count (flow.py:80; only monotonicity in R is tested), removing the hidden-layer saturation clip (gen.py:111; no test or experiment vector ever saturates: 0 of 32 test vectors at F=8/16/32 exceed QMAX before the clip), corrupting the weight feed for rows >= 2 (gen.py:95; no simulation uses R >= 3), and narrowing the accumulator by 2 bits (model.py:45; benign at these magnitudes, max |acc| 204 against a 2^14 limit). The ratio that is the paper's result is computed by untested code.
evidence.craft: Read all 5 modules, the test file, run.py and figure.py. Generators are compact and readable and the testbench is clean. Defects: pyproject.toml:6/8 still names the package chip-systolic-fanin with a 'Batch-size sweep' description; stale docstrings copied forward (gen.py:1 'F-F-4 MLP', gen.py:18 'r + c + 6 compute', baseline_gen.py:3/15 'fan-in 8 ... 8 MAC cycles', baseline_gen.py:49 'Generated by chip_accel.gen'); widths() and _rom() duplicated verbatim in gen.py and baseline_gen.py (copied engine); unclosed file handles (flow.py:45-46, run.py:17, ResourceWarnings in every test run); run.py executes at import, rewrites results.txt on every line and has no CLI or main guard; MAC cycles in the experiment come from a formula although flow.simulate supports simulating them in 3 s.
evidence.claims: Checked 9 claims against results.txt and my recomputations. Backed: table values 245106/188680/1.30 and 458345/360932/1.27; 'All 8 array configurations matched'; 'P=16 ahead of P=8 by 3%' (372045/360932 = 1.031); 'P=16: 217548' at F=16; chip-systolic-hidden ratios 1.22/1.20 (its results.txt:20,28); cycle formulas in Method; the honest 'MAC-lane cycles from the formula' limitation; tests ~30 s. Not backed: README:36 says at F=16 '2x8 (268037) is behind 1x8 (274762)', but 268037 < 274762 and lower is better, so 2x8 is ahead of 1x8; pyproject.toml describes a different project (batch-size sweep). 'beats the best array by 27 to 30%' expresses array/MAC - 1; the MAC engine is 21-23% lower, a loose but common phrasing. Limitations section is careful (one seed, sweep edges, gate counts only, no fabricated chip).
evidence.fitness: A researcher can rerun it in under 4 minutes with apt tools and extend the generators (two later projects did: chip-systolic-p32, chip-mac-lanes). The RTL is bit-exact and cycle-exact, which is a reusable asset. But the result a researcher would cite is weak: one 4-bit toy MLP (quantised accuracy 0.74 at F=32 on 400 test vectors, never reported), one seed, R <= 2, weights compiled into ROM logic, no memory, and it is the fourth one-knob follow-up in a chain (fanin -> hidden -> hidewide -> p32) whose conclusion did not change. Useful as a verified RTL harness, not as a finding.
evidence.domain: Nearest prior work: Kung 1982 (cited, 'not read in full'); SCALE-Sim (Samajdar et al., ISPASS 2020) whose OS runtime model this reproduces; Timeloop/Accelergy (Parashar et al. ISPASS 2019, Wu et al. ICCAD 2019) and Eyeriss (Chen et al. ISCA 2016) dataflow taxonomies; the TPU v1 paper (Jouppi et al. ISCA 2017), which already reports low systolic utilisation on MLPs at small batch. None but Kung is cited. The method is sound as RTL engineering (bit-exact simulation, cycle-exact formula), but departs from accelerator practice in what it compares: with weights compiled into combinational ROM and no SRAM/DRAM, the operand reuse that justifies a systolic array cannot show up in the metric, and R=1 'arrays' are skewed 1-D pipelines that pay C-1 fill cycles per tile against a broadcast MAC engine. My utilisation recomputation shows exactly that: arrays 0.30-0.87 PE utilisation vs MAC engine 0.56-0.95, and ceil(4/C) wastes 50-75% of columns on the 4-wide output layer at C=8/16. The negative result is therefore expected from fill/drain overhead on tiny layers and is not new; a senior reviewer would sign off on the numbers within the stated toy limits, not on the framing as a test of systolic vs MAC architectures.

defects.what: The comparison cannot express what a systolic array is for: weights are compiled into combinational ROM and there is no memory, so operand reuse never enters the metric, and R=1 'arrays' are skewed 1-D pipelines paying C-1 fill cycles per tile against a broadcast MAC engine (PE utilisation 0.30-0.87 vs 0.56-0.95). The negative result follows from fill/drain on tiny layers and is not new (TPU v1, SCALE-Sim); framing as 'does the MAC-engine lead survive' overstates what is tested

The headline metric and ratio are computed by untested code: dropping the /R (run.py:35) or changing the Yosys cell count parse (flow.py:80) leaves every test green; the hidden-layer saturation path and R >= 3 weight feed are never exercised (5 of 7 seeded mutants survived)

verdict: The numbers are right: a full rerun with the same Yosys/Icarus versions reproduces results.txt byte for byte, all 14 cycle counts equal the textbook output-stationary and MAC-lane schedules recomputed independently, all 14 cells x cycles values and both ratios (1.30, 1.27) recompute, and the MAC engine RTL the README says was not simulated at F=16/32 is in fact bit-exact and cycle-exact when simulated. It does not meet the bar: verification is weak where the result lives (the metric code in run.py and the cell-count parse are untested; 5 of 7 seeded mutants survive), one results sentence reverses a comparison (README:36) and the package metadata describes another project. As research it is a verified RTL harness rather than a finding: with weights in ROM logic, no memory and R <= 2, the setup measures fill/drain overhead on tiny layers, so the 'MAC engine wins' result is expected and not new relative to SCALE-Sim and the TPU v1 utilisation results, none of which are cited.
